conclusions: The solver workflows express named return conductors, so an explicit physical return-contract pilot is possible without inventing a catalog model.
SUBGND conductor, lossy bulk substrate, Metal1 return and enclosure/backside boundary are distinct constructs. Neither source names nor common SPICE ground establish equivalence to catalog B.
These reviewed example scripts select fixed layouts. No source-backed parameterized catalog family or independently validated LA/LC/LB/B mapping is established.
A reduced multiport response could be mathematically expressed relative to a chosen common terminal, but algebraic rebasing does not prove that terminal is the physical catalog substrate contact.
next_defensible_work: Select one authenticated geometry and retain exact generator/layout/stackup/port/boundary provenance, without connecting it to the unavailable catalog key.
Specify and validate physical identity of each winding/center-tap/substrate contact and external reference; reject implicit aliasing between Metal1,SUBGND,bulk substrate and global ground.

Only after that contract is resolved, assess solver availability, mesh/convergence checks, passivity/reciprocity, frequency validity and measurement comparison for a separately named experimental reference.
